body:
WHAT
The install format decides how updates work for the life of the install. Windows NSIS installs and AppImages whose own file is writable self-update through electron-updater; Windows portable, macOS dmg, deb and tar.gz are 'assisted' — the click opens the browser on the exact asset for that format. Windows portable is detected by the PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR env var, not by platform; a read-only AppImage falls to assisted instead of failing. Development runs have tier 'none'.

WHY
Handing a portable build the NSIS installer would install a second copy that diverges from the one the user keeps launching; a read-only AppImage cannot rewrite itself.

WHERE
app/main/updates.js — installFormat() (darwin → dmg; win32 → PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR ? portable : nsis; APPIMAGE → AppImage; execPath under /opt/ → deb else tar.gz), installTier() (none when !app.isPackaged; nsis → self; AppImage → fs.accessSync(W_OK) ? self : assisted; else assisted), LINUX_ARCH, assetName(version), startUpdate() branching on state.tier. Names mirror build.portable/nsis/linux/mac artifactName in app/package.json.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. On win32 with PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR set, installFormat() is 'portable', installTier() is 'assisted' and assetName('1.2.3') is 'MAGENTRA-1.2.3-win-portable.exe'; with the variable unset the format is 'nsis', tier 'self' and asset 'MAGENTRA-1.2.3-win-setup.exe'.
2. On linux with APPIMAGE pointing at a writable file the tier is 'self'; with APPIMAGE pointing at a read-only file (accessSync throws) the tier is 'assisted' and assetName is 'MAGENTRA-1.2.3-linux-x86_64.AppImage'.
3. On linux without APPIMAGE, execPath '/opt/MAGENTRA/magentra' yields deb → 'MAGENTRA-1.2.3-linux-amd64.deb', any other path yields tar.gz → 'MAGENTRA-1.2.3-linux-x64.tar.gz'.
4. On darwin arm64 the asset is 'MAGENTRA-1.2.3-mac-arm64.dmg' and on darwin x64 assetName returns null; when app.isPackaged is false the tier is 'none' regardless of platform.
5. Each assetName result matches the artifactName pattern for that target in app/package.json with ${version}/${arch}/${ext} substituted (portable, nsis, linux ${arch} → x86_64/amd64/x64, mac arm64).
